title: AI Regulatory Timeline — EU & UK
subtitle: Key compliance deadlines and regulatory milestones for AI-enabled products entering European markets

events.label: 1 Aug 2024
events.title: EU AI Act Enters Into Force
events.description: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 enters into force. Organisations begin preparing compliance programmes, AI inventories, risk assessments and governance structures. The world's first comprehensive AI-specific legal framework becomes law.
events.impact: Foundation — all subsequent deadlines derive from this date.

events.label: 2 Feb 2025
events.title: EU: Prohibited Practices & AI Literacy
events.description: Article 5 prohibited practices become applicable. AI literacy obligations also take effect. Certain AI uses are now outright banned across the EU.
events.impact: Companies must ensure no prohibited AI practices are deployed in EU markets.
events.linkLabel: EU AI Act Desk: Article 5 Prohibited Practices

events.label: 2 Aug 2025
events.title: EU: GPAI Obligations Apply
events.description: General-Purpose AI (GPAI) model obligations become applicable, including technical documentation requirements, copyright compliance policies, and training data summaries. Foundation model developers face new regulatory duties.
events.impact: Foundation model providers must have documentation and copyright compliance in place.
events.linkLabel: EC Digital Strategy: GPAI Obligations Factsheet

events.label: Late 2025
events.title: UK: ICO ADM Consultation & Code of Practice Begins
events.description: ICO consultation on updated guidance for automated decision-making (ADM) and profiling, including AI in recruitment and public services. Work begins toward a statutory AI and ADM Code of Practice under the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025.
events.impact: UK companies should monitor and engage with consultation. ADM governance expectations are rising.

events.label: Mar 2026
events.title: UK: Copyright & AI Report Published
events.description: UK Government confirms the broad text-and-data-mining exception is not being taken forward. Licensing, provenance and record-keeping become the practical foundation for lawful AI development. No replacement legislation introduced.
events.impact: AI developers must establish licensing/permissions for training data. Broad TDM exception is off the table.
events.linkLabel: GOV.UK: Report on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence

events.label: 7 May 2026
events.title: EU: Digital Omnibus on AI — Political Agreement
events.description: Political agreement reached on Digital Omnibus amendments to the AI Act. Adjusts compliance timelines for certain high-risk AI systems and refines scope. Prohibits AI 'nudification' apps and non-consensual intimate imagery.
events.impact: Sets the stage for the Dec 2027 high-risk system deadline.
events.linkLabel: EC Press Release: Digital Omnibus Agreement

events.label: 23 Jul 2026
events.title: EU: Google Fined €890M Under DMA
events.description: European Commission fines Google (Alphabet) €890 million under the Digital Markets Act: €460M for self-preferencing in Google Search, €430M for anti-steering restrictions on Google Play. Demonstrates the enforcement posture for digital regulation.
events.impact: Strong signal that the Commission will levy substantial penalties. AI Act enforcement likely to follow similar pattern.
events.linkLabel: EC Press Release: Google DMA Fine

events.label: 2 Aug 2026
events.title: EU: Major AI Act Obligations Become Operational ⚠️
events.description: The most significant operational deadline. Most AI Act obligations become applicable: transparency duties, provider obligations, deployer obligations, and enforcement mechanisms. Article 50 transparency requirements operational for newly deployed systems. Chatbots must identify as AI, synthetic content must carry machine-readable labelling, deepfake disclosure processes must be operational. Directly impacts products such as MagicDawn, GVoice, AI Voice Studio.
events.impact: CRITICAL. Companies selling AI-enabled products into the EU must have substantially operational compliance programmes by this date.

events.label: 2 Dec 2026
events.title: EU: Article 50 Deadline & New Prohibitions
events.description: Article 50 compliance deadline for generative AI systems already on the market before August 2026. New prohibitions relating to non-consensual intimate imagery and AI-generated CSAM become applicable. Transitional period for existing products ends.
events.impact: All generative AI products on EU market must meet transparency requirements by this date.
events.linkLabel: AI Act Explorer: Article 50 Full Text

events.label: 9 Dec 2026
events.title: EU: New Product Liability Directive Implementation
events.description: Member States must implement the New Product Liability Directive (2024/2853). Software, including AI, now explicitly qualifies as a product. Strict liability applies to AI system providers. Companies should review regulatory compliance, product liability risk profiles, insurance coverage, and supply chain agreements.
events.impact: AI software providers face strict product liability in the EU. Supply chain review essential.
events.linkLabel: EC: New Product Liability Directive Overview

events.label: Late 2026
events.title: UK: Digital Replicas Consultation Expected
events.description: UK government expected to consult on digital replicas. Likely to have direct relevance to product design, talent agreements, consent management and reputational risk controls in games and media.
events.impact: Games and media companies using AI-generated likenesses should prepare for new requirements.
events.linkLabel: GOV.UK: Copyright & AI Report (Digital Replicas section)

events.label: May 2027
events.title: EU: DMA Cloud Market Investigation Report
events.description: European Commission stakeholder roundtable report expected on cloud computing services under Article 19 of the Digital Markets Act. May influence competition requirements and cloud-provider obligations in Europe.
events.impact: Cloud providers supporting AI deployment may face new market obligations.

events.label: 2 Dec 2027
events.title: EU: Annex III High-Risk AI Systems Become Applicable ⚠️
events.description: Requirements for many Annex III high-risk AI systems become applicable. Covers standalone high-risk systems in employment (recruitment), education (assessment), public services, financial services (credit scoring), and certain law-enforcement applications. Note: this does NOT postpone prohibited-practice rules, GPAI obligations, transparency requirements, or AI-literacy requirements.
events.impact: CRITICAL. Companies with AI systems in recruitment, education, finance, or public-sector use cases must comply with full high-risk requirements.
events.linkLabel: Regulation AI: Annex III High-Risk Categories & Deadlines

events.label: 2 Aug 2028
events.title: EU: Annex I Product-Embedded High-Risk AI — Full Application ⚠️
events.description: High-risk AI embedded within regulated products covered by Annex I legislation becomes fully subject to AI Act requirements. Includes AI integrated into regulated machinery, transport systems, medical products, and industrial technologies. The EU compliance framework reaches near-full implementation.
events.impact: CRITICAL. Full AI Act coverage. All high-risk AI systems in regulated products must comply.
events.linkLabel: Regulation AI: Complete AI Act Compliance Timeline

events.label: By 2030
events.title: UK & EU: Expected Developments Through 2030
events.description: Expected developments include: increasing UK AI legislation (additional regulator powers, statutory reporting, sector-specific requirements), expansion of AI auditing requirements (independent model audits, algorithmic impact assessments, bias testing), increased liability for AI-generated decisions, AI supply chain governance, and convergence around global standards (transparency, accountability, safety testing, human oversight).
events.impact: Build governance structures now — don't wait for legislation. The organisations most likely to succeed are those building compliance before it becomes mandatory.
